record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: For retarded time-delay systems, is it sufficient to require a pointwise dissipation inequality of the form |x(0)| ≥ χ(‖u‖_U) ⇒ V̇_u(x) ≤ −α(|x(0)|) in order to conclude ISS? Equivalently, can the stronger Lyapunov-Krasovskii hypothesis V(x) ≥ χ(|u(0)|) ⇒ V̇_u(x) ≤ −α(|x(0)|) be weakened to a condition that depends only on the current state magnitude and full input norm?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a retarded nonlinear time-delay system of the form
    ẋ(t) = f(x_t, u(t)),    t ≥ 0,
where, for some maximum delay r > 0, the state history is x_t ∈ C([−r,0]; ℝ^n) defined by x_t(θ) = x(t+θ), the input u: [0,∞) → U takes values in a normed input space (U, |·|_U) and is locally essentially bounded, and f: C([−r,0]; ℝ^n) × U → ℝ^n is locally Lipschitz and ensures forward completeness of solutions. The system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K_∞ such that
    |x(t)| ≤ β(‖x_0‖_C, t) + γ(‖u‖_{L^∞(0,t;U)})
for every initial condition x_0 ∈ C([−r,0]; ℝ^n), every admissible input u, and every t ≥ 0.

Let V: C([−r,0]; ℝ^n) → ℝ_{≥0} be a continuous Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional that is locally Lipschitz on bounded sets, and assume there exist ψ_1, ψ_2 ∈ K_∞ with
    ψ_1(|φ(0)|) ≤ V(φ) ≤ ψ_2(‖φ‖_C)    for all φ ∈ C([−r,0]; ℝ^n).
For an absolutely continuous solution x(·) corresponding to input u, denote by V̇_u(x_t) the upper-right Dini derivative of t ↦ V(x_t) along trajectories.

Question. Do there exist α, χ ∈ K_∞ such that the pointwise dissipation implication
    |x(0)| ≥ χ(‖u‖_U)    ⟹    V̇_u(x_t) ≤ −α(|x(0)|)
(where |x(0)| denotes the magnitude of the current state value x_t(0) and ‖u‖_U denotes the essential supremum norm of the input) is by itself sufficient to imply that the system is ISS? Equivalently, can the standard Lyapunov–Krasovskii sufficient condition
    V(x_t) ≥ χ(|u(t)|)    ⟹    V̇_u(x_t) ≤ −α(|x(0)|)
be weakened to the above condition, which depends only on the current state magnitude and the full input norm?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is generally regarded as still open in full generality. Partial results exist: the analogous statement for integral ISS (iISS) has been answered positively, and recent work shows that if the Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional with pointwise dissipation also yields uniform global stability, then ISS follows. A 2026 superposition-based approach gives further partial progress, but no complete proof or counterexample for the full conjecture has been published.

status_evidence.title: A superposition approach for the ISS Lyapunov-Krasovskii theorem with pointwise dissipation
status_evidence.snippet: if the Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional that dissipates pointwisely can also be used to establish uniform global stability, then the ISS property holds
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: pointwise dissipation plus uniform global stability implies ISS, but the full conjecture remains unproven.

status_evidence.title: Is a point-wise dissipation rate enough to show ISS for time-delay systems?
status_evidence.snippet: point-wise dissipation rate enough to show ISS for time-delay systems
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly framed as an open problem with only partial answers.

status_evidence.title: Lyapunov-Krasovskii Characterizations of Integral Input-to-State Stability of Delay Systems With Nonstrict Dissipation Rates
status_evidence.snippet: Lyapunov-Krasovskii characterizations of iISS with nonstrict dissipation
status_evidence.claim: The closely related iISS version has been resolved positively.
